newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says personnel changes not imminent.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says personnel changes not imminent.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Tuesday there were no immediate plans for personnel changes, despite a news agency report that a former deputy finance minister could take up a senior post.
The Slovak official news agency TASR said Jozef Magula, replaced earlier in the day, "would (probably) take a high function in the National Bank of Slovakia" -- the country's central bank.
Three of the eight seats on the bank's governing board are vacant and are the subject of talks with the government.

"No personnel changes are taking place here at the moment," Jan Onda, a NBS spokesman, told Reuters. "Though there have been ongoing talks with the government on the three vacant seats in the NBS's governing board".
The three seats have been vacant since the end of December when the four-year term of Jozef Makuch, a head of the NBS's Monetary Studies Institute, expired. Two seats had vacant for some time.
"However, the board has a quorum even with only the current five members," Onda said, adding that no deadline had been set for the new members' appointment.

The government appoints the board members and its two chief executive directors based on a proposal by the governor. The President appoints the governor and two vice-governors, based on government proposals and with parliament's approval.

Opposition politicians have warned that reshuflles in the NBS's governing board may follow a recent monetary tightening and last week's reshuffle in the board of directors of Investicna a Rozvojova Banka a.s. (IRB), the country's third largest commercial bank. -- Tatiana Vacova, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
